messages.author: 11ce49b663049f2e
messages.subject: Re: Java Issue??
parts:
Hi, 

Maybe try setting memory.limit higher..
Check how much is currently allocated with memory.limit()
Check how much is currently in use with memory.size()

To change the maximum memory limit you could do it two ways.
1. 
In JGR use:
memory.limit(4096)
to allocate 4096 (~4Gb) to Java. 

2.
To have it always allocate more ram, in Rprofile.site add something like..

utils::memory.limit(10240)

this would allocate 10240mb to Java on startup.

Of course, you can't allocate anything higher than the amount of system ram you have.. 

good luck.

messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Re: Java Issue??
parts:
This is a Java out of memory error, not an R one, so you need to set the memory higher on launching JGR. There is no elegant way to do this. starting R and running

library(JGR)
launchJGR(javaArgs="-Xss10m")

will launch JGR with each Java thread getting 10 MB.

Ian

messages.subject: Re: Java Issue??
parts:
This is a Java out of memory error, not an R one, so you need to set the memory higher on launching JGR. There is no elegant way to do this. starting R and running

library(JGR)
launchJGR(javaArgs="-Xss10m")

will launch JGR with each Java thread getting 10 MB.

Ian
On Oct 1, 2015, at 4:19 PM, sinha...@gmail.com wrote:

I get the same error if I try to load file. I tried increasing the memory limit to 4GB but R still crashes. 
All I do is launch JGR and try to open data, it crashes before I even select the datafile.

Any suggestions? Thanks!




On Sunday, 15 March 2015 17:28:31 UTC-7, Kieran Short wrote:
Hi, 

Maybe try setting memory.limit higher..
Check how much is currently allocated with memory.limit()
Check how much is currently in use with memory.size()

To change the maximum memory limit you could do it two ways.
1. 
In JGR use:
memory.limit(4096)
to allocate 4096 (~4Gb) to Java. 

2.
To have it always allocate more ram, in Rprofile.site add something like..

utils::memory.limit(10240)

this would allocate 10240mb to Java on startup.

Of course, you can't allocate anything higher than the amount of system ram you have.. 

good luck.
